problem:
A certain company produces three types of ground coffee: fine, medium, and coarse. The following table describes how the number of customers changes between the three types of ground coffee each year:

|  |  | From: |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Fine** | **Medium** | **Coarse** |
| To: | **Fine** | $0.5$ | $0.2$ | $0.2$ |
| **Medium** | $0.3$ | $0.6$ | $0.4$ |  |
| **Coarse** | $0.2$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ |  |

For example, $30%$ of fine ground coffee customers switch to medium ground coffee each year, and $20%$ of coarse ground coffee customers switch to fine ground coffee.

Currently, $300\,000$ customers buy fine ground coffee, $500\,000$ customers buy medium ground coffee, and $200\,000$ customers buy coarse ground coffee. How many customers will purchase fine ground coffee in one year? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.
